partners.mechanism_chain: DNAH5 (HGNC:2700) —DISRUPTS→ Ciliary and flagellar structure and motility (GO:0005847); Ciliary and flagellar structure and motility (GO:0005847) —LEADS_TO→ Primary ciliary dyskinesia (MONDO:0016575); TUBB2B (HGNC:12470) —DISRUPTS→ Cytoskeleton organization (GO:0007010); Cytoskeleton organization (GO:0007010) —LEADS_TO→ Complex cortical dysplasia with other brain malformations 7 (MONDO:0012399); Ciliary and flagellar structure and motility (GO:0005847) —BINDS→ Cytoskeleton organization (GO:0007010). Loss-of-function mutations in DNAH5 disrupt the ciliary and flagellar structure and motility, leading to primary ciliary dyskinesia. Concurrently, mutations in TUBB2B disrupt the cytoskeleton organization, which is essential for neuronal development and can lead to complex cortical dysplasia. The cilia and flagella (n2) are themselves complex cytoskeletal structures, thus their proper function is intrinsically linked to overall cytoskeleton organization (n3), creating a point of convergence.

partners.mechanism_chain: DNAH5 (HGNC:2707) —LEADS_TO→ Primary ciliary dyskinesia (MONDO:0016575); CENPF (HGNC:16971) —DISRUPTS→ Centrosome and Centriole Biogenesis (GO:0005814); Centrosome and Centriole Biogenesis (GO:0005814) —LEADS_TO→ Houge-Janssens syndrome 2 (MONDO:0014605).
